canonical encoding for the execution profile and for the result, including traps

hazards.summary: The repo sits on a fuse mount with one-second mtime granularity. Python validates cached bytecode against source mtime and size, so a same-length edit landing in the same second as the previous run leaves Python executing stale bytecode. A run can edit code, see tests pass, and commit a change that never ran.
hazards.mitigation: Gate scripts export PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX to keep bytecode off the mount. Existing .pyc files under the mount resist deletion; bump source mtimes with touch instead.

agents.name: OpenALP conformance

mandate.statement: The goal is not to make OpenALP larger. The goal is to make OpenALP impossible to replace.
admission_test: Does ordinary tool calling already solve this?
Does this duplicate existing protocol behavior?
Does this strengthen OpenALP's unique thesis?
mandate.rule: A feature that does not strengthen exactly one named pillar is rejected. A feature duplicated by MCP, A2A or ordinary tool calling is removed unless OpenALP requires it internally.
mandate.position: OpenALP is not an agent transport and must stop behaving like one. It is the payload that rides inside MCP tool results and A2A artifacts: the thing that turns an opaque result into a deterministic, verifiable, replayable computation. Competing with MCP or A2A on delivery is a fight OpenALP loses.
mandate.evidence_reviewed: 2026-08-27, against MCP spec 2026-07-28 and the current A2A specification.

audit.finding: The transport layer is 783 lines. The deterministic core it exists to serve is 441. The duplicated surface is now larger than the unique thesis.

verdicts.feature: Deterministic module format (.alp), reference VM, determinism report
verdicts.reason: Nothing in MCP or A2A carries a portable, byte-exact executable representation. MCP tools are opaque endpoints; A2A artifacts are generic content containers with no executable semantics. This is the only thing OpenALP has that cannot be obtained elsewhere.

verdicts.feature: Checksum and signature manifests over the module
verdicts.reason: MCP 2026-07-28 contains no cryptographic signature, integrity verification or signed execution artifact concept. A2A authenticates the channel, not the computation. Signing a portable executable artifact is unoccupied ground.
Directly defends the pillar. Without it the format is validated only against itself.

A2A task IDs are server-generated and opaque; deduplication is MAY, via messageId. A computation identity derived from payload content is stronger, and is a property of determinism rather than of delivery. Rename from delivery envelope to computation identity.

verdicts.feature: Per-stream ordering, sequence contiguity, pending flush
verdicts.reason: A2A mandates that implementations deliver events in generation order regardless of binding. Every queue and transport solves this. Strengthens no pillar.

A2A TaskState already defines working, input-required, auth-required, completed, failed, canceled and rejected. MCP has a tasks extension with polling. This is a reimplementation with different spelling.

A2A deliberately leaves retry to implementations, so this is not duplicated by spec. It is still solved by every transport in existence and strengthens no pillar. Rejected on pillar grounds, not duplication grounds.

verdicts.feature: Deadlines, logical clock, clock policy, quantization
verdicts.reason: Same reasoning as retry. The determinism argument that motivated the logical clock exists only because the deadline feature exists; removing the feature removes the problem it solves.

verdicts.verdict: remove as feature, retain as property
verdicts.reason: Content-derived identity makes deduplication free for anyone who wants it. Shipping a receipt store means owning operating state OpenALP has no business owning.

verdicts.feature: Agent identity, sender attribution, key rotation, revocation
verdicts.reason: A2A declares API key, HTTP basic and bearer, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and mutual TLS in agent cards. MCP 2026-07-28 hardened authorization with RFC 9207 issuer validation and Client ID Metadata Documents. Building sender identity is rebuilding solved infrastructure badly. Signing the module stays; authenticating the sender goes.
An MCP registry exists. More fundamentally, content addressing is what a registry is for: if modules are addressed by hash, the registry is a cache someone else can run.
Strengthens no pillar. Not duplicated, simply out of scope. Removed from the roadmap entirely rather than deferred, because deferring it implies it returns.

Observability is solved by OpenTelemetry and A2A task history. A deterministic trace a third party can independently replay to the same hash is not observability, it is proof. Only the proof form survives.

An A2A Artifact is a generic container with no executable semantics; an MCP tool result is opaque content. Carrying a verifiable OpenALP module inside either makes OpenALP complementary rather than competing, which is the only position it survives in.

phase_discipline: Work only on tasks belonging to active_phase. A task from a later phase is not eligible however attractive it looks. Phases close when every task in them is done and the gate is green; the human decides when to open the next one.

determinism_findings.claim_under_test: same artifact + same canonical input + same execution profile = same canonical result hash
determinism_findings.verdict: The invariant does not currently hold across implementations. `alp determinism report` proves repeatability within one Python process; it says nothing about agreement between two conforming implementations. Every finding below was reproduced by running the reference VM.

findings.observed: Arithmetic uses Python arbitrary-precision integers. 127 squared four times yields a 112-bit value (4579937329576774398276408998492161).
findings.consequence: Any implementation in C, Rust, Go or WASM overflows at 64 bits and produces a different result for the same artifact. There is no defined width, no defined overflow behaviour.
findings.recommended_resolution: Adopt i64 two's complement with wrapping add/sub/mul, following the WASM numeric model — the most heavily studied deterministic execution spec available.

findings.observed: DIV uses Python floor division. -7 / 2 evaluates to -4.
findings.consequence: C, Rust, Go and WASM all truncate toward zero and produce -3. Silent divergence on every negative division.
findings.recommended_resolution: Truncate toward zero. Trap on divide-by-zero and on INT64_MIN / -1, both as canonical traps.

findings.observed: PUSH_CONST sign-extends an 8-bit operand, so operand 200 becomes -56. PRINT_CHAR requires 0..255 and rejects negatives.
findings.consequence: Byte values 128-255 are unreachable from a constant. The two width models contradict each other inside one instruction set.
findings.recommended_resolution: State one width model: operands sign-extend i8 to i64, and PRINT_CHAR emits value & 0xFF as a total function with no trap.

findings.observed: The same module halts normally under a 1000-step budget and traps under a 5-step budget. max_steps is a Python keyword argument, present in neither the module nor any declared profile.
findings.consequence: The step budget silently changes the result of an identical artifact, so it must be part of the execution profile the invariant names, or the invariant is unprovable.
findings.recommended_resolution: Make the step budget a required, canonically encoded field of the execution profile, and include it in the hash preimage.

findings.observed: Failures raise VMError with free-text messages such as 'stack underflow in ADD: need 2, have 0'.
findings.consequence: A failing execution has no canonical result, so it cannot be hashed or compared. Two implementations cannot agree that they failed the same way.
findings.recommended_resolution: Define a closed set of canonical trap codes. A trap is a normal, hashable outcome, not an absence of one.

findings.observed: The reference VM has no input mechanism at all; run_module takes a module and a step budget.
findings.consequence: The target invariant names 'canonical input', which does not exist. Either an input model is defined or the spec must state that modules are closed computations and drop the term.

findings.observed: Output accumulates Python str characters via chr(), producing code points rather than bytes.
findings.consequence: Canonical output is ambiguous between a byte string and a text string with an encoding. Hashes computed over it would differ by implementation language.
findings.recommended_resolution: Output is a byte string. Canonical encoding is the raw bytes; any text interpretation is out of scope.

findings.observed: Execution is single-threaded with no concurrency primitives.
findings.consequence: Not a defect, but the specification must state it normatively so a future implementation cannot introduce parallelism and claim conformance.
findings.recommended_resolution: State that the execution model is strictly sequential and that no conforming implementation may observe or introduce concurrency within a single execution.

on: F1 integer width and overflow semantics
F6 input model: closed computations or defined input
